tagline: A wall of skyscrapers between green peaks and a glittering harbour, Hong Kong packs dim sum halls, double-decker trams, neon markets and island escapes into one compact city. It is ranked #15 on Time Out's Best Cities 2026 list.
overview: Hong Kong was a scatter of fishing villages until it became a British colony in 1841. It returned to China in 1997 under the 'one country, two systems' framework, and that East-meets-West mix still defines it, from Cantonese temples to British-style pubs.

The classic view is from Victoria Peak, reached by the historic Peak Tram. Down below, the Star Ferry has crossed Victoria Harbour since 1888, and the Tsim Sha Tsui promenade faces the famous skyline. On Lantau Island, the Ngong Ping 360 cable car climbs to the giant Tian Tan Buddha.

Food is a sport here: morning dim sum, roast goose, egg tarts and late-night wonton noodles. Markets like Temple Street and the Ladies' Market glow after dark, and a third of the territory is country park, with hikes like the Dragon's Back minutes from the towers.

funFacts.title: MORE SKYSCRAPERS THAN ANYWHERE
funFacts.text: Hong Kong has more buildings over 150 metres tall than any other city in the world.

funFacts.title: THE STAR FERRY
funFacts.text: The green-and-white Star Ferry has crossed Victoria Harbour since 1888 and still costs pocket change.

funFacts.title: DING DING TRAMS
funFacts.text: Hong Kong's double-decker trams have run since 1904 and form the largest double-decker tram fleet in service.

funFacts.title: A GIANT BUDDHA
funFacts.text: The Tian Tan Buddha on Lantau Island is about 34 metres tall and is reached by climbing 268 steps.

funFacts.title: THE LONGEST ESCALATOR
funFacts.text: The Central–Mid-Levels escalator system is the world's longest outdoor covered escalator network.

funFacts.title: FENG SHUI TOWERS
funFacts.text: Several skyscrapers have holes, called 'dragon gates', so dragons can pass from the hills to the sea.

funFacts.title: MOSTLY GREEN
funFacts.text: Despite the dense skyline, roughly 40 percent of Hong Kong's land is protected country park.

funFacts.title: A HANDOVER CITY
funFacts.text: Hong Kong was British for 156 years before returning to China on 1 July 1997.

funFacts.title: OCTOPUS CARD
funFacts.text: Launched in 1997, the Octopus card was one of the world's first contactless payment cards.
